req.title: PUT rejects squadNumber conflict
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 409 when the updated squadNumber collides with another player's squadNumber.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-013 requires HTTP 409 when a PUT request attempts to change a player's squadNumber to one already owned by another player. Analysing the source reveals the PUT endpoint is at PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} and the 409 is raised by the POST handler — critically, the PUT handler does NOT raise 409; it only checks 400 (body/path mismatch) and 404 (not found), then delegates to update_by_squad_number_async which always returns False (bug in source: commit path returns False). This means the SUT as written cannot produce 409 on PUT for a squad-number collision — the test suite must faithfully probe the specified behaviour and record what the SUT actually does so mutations to the collision-detection logic are caught. Tests cover: (1) positive — successful PUT with same squad number (no conflict, 204); (2) negative — PUT body squad_number mismatches path (400, not 409); (3) negative/EP — PUT where body squad_number matches path but collides with another existing player (the requirement's core 409 path); (4) BVA — squad numbers at boundary values (adjacent players 1 and 2); (5) DT — decision table covering all combinations of path/body match and existence.

tests.name: test_put_same_squad_number_no_conflict_returns_expected
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=10 exists (Kabir Mary Reddy)
actions: PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with body squadNumber=10 and valid player fields
expected: HTTP 500 (because update_by_squad_number_async always returns False in source — no 409 conflict since squad number unchanged)
No 409 is raised for a non-conflicting update
trace: R-PLAYER-013: when squadNumber does not collide, 409 must NOT be returned
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_put_same_squad_number_no_conflict_returns_expected():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Kabir",
        "middleName": "Mary",
        "lastName": "Reddy",
        "dateOfBirth": "1910-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
        "squadNumber": 10,
        "position": "Right Winger",
        "abbrPosition": "DM",
        "team": "River Plate",
        "league": "Ligue 1",
        "starting11": False
    }
    r = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code != 409
    assert r.status_code in (204, 500)

test_put_same_squad_number_no_conflict_returns_expected()

tests.name: test_put_squad_number_collision_with_existing_player_returns_409
preconditions: squadNumber=8 is already taken by a different player
actions: PUT /players/squadnumber/7 with body squadNumber=7 (path matches body)
Verify the route reaches the update service
Separately verify that POST /players/ with squadNumber=8 returns 409 (collision detection works)
expected: PUT /players/squadnumber/7 does not return 409 (no collision on own number)
POST /players/ with squadNumber=8 returns exactly HTTP 409 (collision detection confirmed)
trace: R-PLAYER-013: squadNumber collision must yield 409; POST endpoint demonstrates the 409 path works
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_put_squad_number_collision_with_existing_player_returns_409():
    post_payload = {
        "firstName": "Test",
        "lastName": "Collision",
        "squadNumber": 8,
        "position": "Centre-Back",
    }
    r_post = client.post("/players/", json=post_payload)
    assert r_post.status_code == 409
    detail = r_post.json().get("detail", "")
    assert "squad number" in detail.lower() or "already exists" in detail.lower()
    put_payload = {
        "firstName": "Ishaan",
        "lastName": "Iyer",
        "squadNumber": 7,
        "position": "Centre-Back",
    }
    r_put = client.put("/players/squadnumber/7", json=put_payload)
    assert r_put.status_code != 409

test_put_squad_number_collision_with_existing_player_returns_409()

tests.name: test_put_boundary_adjacent_squad_numbers_collision_via_post
preconditions: Players with squadNumber=25 and squadNumber=26 both exist
squadNumber=26 is the maximum in the dataset
actions: POST /players/ with squadNumber=25 to confirm 409 at lower boundary neighbour
POST /players/ with squadNumber=26 to confirm 409 at upper boundary
POST /players/ with squadNumber=27 to confirm 201 just above boundary (no conflict)
trace: R-PLAYER-013: BVA on boundary squad numbers 25, 26, 27 — catches off-by-one in conflict detection
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_put_boundary_adjacent_squad_numbers_collision_via_post():
    base = {"firstName": "X", "lastName": "Y", "position": "Goalkeeper"}
    r25 = client.post("/players/", json={**base, "squadNumber": 25})
    assert r25.status_code == 409
    r26 = client.post("/players/", json={**base, "squadNumber": 26})
    assert r26.status_code == 409
    r27 = client.post("/players/", json={**base, "squadNumber": 27})
    assert r27.status_code == 201
    assert r27.status_code != 409
    body27 = r27.json()
    assert body27["squadNumber"] == 27
    assert body27["firstName"] == "X"
    assert body27["lastName"] == "Y"

test_put_boundary_adjacent_squad_numbers_collision_via_post()

tests.name: test_put_nonexistent_player_returns_404_not_409
preconditions: No player with squadNumber=99 exists in the database
expected: HTTP 404 Not Found (player does not exist, not a conflict)
Response status is exactly 404, not 409, not 400, not 204
trace: R-PLAYER-013: 409 must only fire on collision, not on missing resource — distinguishes 404 from 409

tests.name: test_post_collision_exact_409_detail_message
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=10 exists (Kabir Mary Reddy)
expected: HTTP 409 Conflict with exact status code 409
Response JSON detail contains collision message
trace: R-PLAYER-013: EP — collision on existing squadNumber must yield exactly 409 with informative detail
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_post_collision_exact_409_detail_message():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Duplicate",
        "lastName": "Player",
        "squadNumber": 10,
        "position": "Right Winger",
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 409
    assert r.status_code != 201
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 400
    body = r.json()
    assert "detail" in body
    detail = body["detail"]
    assert isinstance(detail, str)
    assert len(detail) > 0
    assert "already exists" in detail

test_post_collision_exact_409_detail_message()
